# Volume 2 — XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

School’s final day arrived and passed. An impressive “semi-annual examination” took place, and the students of Nell performed exceptionally well. When it ended, they presented her with a presentation speech and a writing desk. Every girl and woman in attendance wept, and several boys were teased about crying as well in the time that followed, even though they constantly disputed it.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0000 }

In each other's company, Mrs. Gorham Pullen, Mrs. Peter Mott, and Mrs. William Bell made their way back to their houses while discussing the matter.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0001 }

“Since the youngsters appear to be so fond of Nell, her departure strikes me as an absolute shame,” uttered Mrs. Peter Mott with a sigh, given her inclination to sigh about all matters and to conclude even her humorous remarks in that manner. “Of course,” she quickly put in, “it is known to us all that our teacher for the upcoming year will likewise be a fine one.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0002 }

“I have no doubt that Odette will perform her duty,” Mrs. Pullen stated with a degree of stiffness. “She probably will not share quite as many fairy stories with the children or devote such a large amount of time to wandering through the woods beside them. Nevertheless, her name appears on the Inspector’s Roll of Honor, and the individuals from Stonebridge are deeply upset about her departure.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0003 }

“Nell going to college makes me real glad,” Mrs. Bell stated. “It is something she has always wished for, and for her, it will be a splendid thing.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0004 }

“Indeed, I am uncertain,” stated Mrs. Pullen, who had made up her mind not to concur entirely with anyone on that occasion. “It appears to me that additional schooling is unnecessary for Nell. Provided his fascination with her persists until his graduation, she is likely to wed Hugh Carrow, which makes me wonder how Latin and Greek will benefit her at that point. Should higher education instruct a person in the handling of a husband, her attendance could perhaps be justified.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0005 }

According to the rumors in Brierley, Mrs. Gorham Pullen had failed to figure out how to handle her “man,” which meant that the Pullen home could hardly be called a pattern of marital bliss.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0006 }

“I notice that the Presbytery is considering the Port Marlow call to Mr. Wace,” Mrs. Bell stated. “I guess that implies he will be leaving us shortly.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0007 }

“It won’t be prior to September that they depart,” Mrs. Mott remarked. “Their absence will be deeply felt by everyone . . . even if I constantly held the opinion that Mrs. Wace’s attire was somewhat overly showy for the spouse of a clergyman. However, every single one of us has flaws. Did you observe Mr. Pettifer’s tidy and comfortable appearance today? Never have I witnessed a person so completely transformed. Every Sunday sees him attending church, and he has contributed to the minister’s pay.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0008 }

“Is that not Cedric Stanhope who has become such a large boy?” inquired Mrs. Pullen. “He was so small for his years upon his arrival here. Truly, I scarcely recognized him today. He is starting to resemble his father quite a bit.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0009 }

“That boy is intelligent,” Mrs. Bell stated.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0010 }

“He possesses sufficient intelligence, yet” . . . Mrs. Pullen dropped her tone . . . “I think he recounts odd tales. Gracie returned from school a day during last week carrying the most absurd nonsense he had shared with her regarding folks residing down at the beach . . . tales wherein not a single statement could possibly be true, as you are aware. I instructed Gracie to disbelieve them, whereupon she stated that Cedric had no intention for her to do so. However, if that was not his purpose, why did he relate them to her?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0011 }

“Nell thinks Cedric is exceptionally clever,” Mrs. Mott said.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0012 }

“He might be. They Americans are completely unpredictable,” Mrs. Pullen stated. Mrs. Pullen’s sole familiarity with the term “genius” originated from the informal habit of labeling any peculiar person “a queer genius.” She likely believed, along with Mary Joe, that it signified someone who was mentally unbalanced.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0013 }

Returning to the classroom, Nell sat by herself at her desk, just like she had sat when school started for the first time two years earlier, resting her face against her hand while her tearful eyes gazed longingly through the window toward the Lake of Glassy Waters. Because her heart was aching so deeply from saying goodbye to her students, college briefly seemed to have forfeited all its appeal. She could still sense Annetta Bell’s arms wrapped around her neck and hear the girl’s young cry, “I’ll never love any teacher as much as you, Miss Harcourt, never, never.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0014 }

Over a period of two years, her labor had been diligent and devoted as she committed numerous errors and gained wisdom through them. A recompense had come to her. Something had been imparted by her to her students, yet her own feeling was that a far greater amount had been imparted by them to her . . . insights into affection, emotional restraint, blameless intelligence, knowledge of young minds. It might be that she had failed in “inspiring” her students with any extraordinary aspirations, but through the influence of her lovely disposition rather than through her diligent instructions, she had shown them that as they faced the upcoming years, it was proper and essential to exist with nobility and elegance, clinging tightly to honesty, politeness, and benevolence, while steering clear of everything possessing a hint of untruthfulness, petty behavior, and crudeness. It was possible they had no awareness of acquiring those principles; nevertheless, those concepts would be recalled and applied by them a great deal of time after the capital of Afghanistan and the dates of the Wars of the Roses had faded from their minds.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0015 }

“A further part of my existence has come to an end,” Nell uttered out loud, while securing her writing table. The situation made her feel truly sorrowful; nevertheless, she found a small amount of solace in the romantic notion of that “closed chapter.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0016 }

During the beginning of her break, Nell passed two weeks at Echo Cottage, which brought enjoyment to all involved.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0017 }

She accompanied Miss Rosalind on a shopping trip to town and convinced her to purchase a new organdy dress; afterwards, they experienced the thrill of cutting and sewing it as a team, with the joyful Belinda the Fourth basting and sweeping up scraps. Miss Rosalind had stated that she was unable to feel much enthusiasm for anything, yet the glimmer returned to her eyes concerning her lovely garment.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0018 }

“How silly and light-headed I have to be,” she uttered with a sigh. “It makes me thoroughly embarrassed that an untested gown . . . even one made of forget-me-not organdy . . . can thrill me in this way, whereas a clean conscience plus an increased donation to Foreign Missions failed to accomplish it.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0019 }

Halfway through her stay, Nell returned to Grey Shutters for one day so that she could repair the stockings belonging to the twins and answer the collection of questions Robin had saved up. During the evening, she walked toward the shore road for the purpose of visiting Cedric Stanhope. When she went past the square, low window belonging to the Stanhope sitting room, she caught sight of Cedric sitting upon the lap of someone; however, immediately afterward he rushed out through the hall.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0020 }

“Oh, Miss Harcourt,” he exclaimed with excitement, “you can’t imagine what took place! Something truly wonderful. Father has arrived . . . only imagine that! Father has arrived! Step right inside. Father, this is my lovely teacher. You understand, father.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0021 }

Smiling, Stephen Stanhope stepped ahead to greet Nell. With iron-gray hair, sunken dark blue eyes, and a powerful, sorrowful countenance remarkably shaped around the brow and chin, he was a well-favored, tall man of middle age. Nell felt a wave of deep contentment as she reflected that his face was precisely right for a romantic hero. Discovering that a person who should be a hero was stooped or bald, or in some other manner devoid of masculine attractiveness, was exceedingly disheartening. Had the subject of Miss Rosalind’s romance failed to look his role, Nell would have deemed it terrible.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0022 }

“Thus, here is the ‘beautiful teacher’ belonging to my small boy, about whom so many things have reached my ears,” Mr. Stanhope uttered, shaking my hand warmly. “Because Cedric’s missives have contained so much about you, Miss Harcourt, my feeling is that our acquaintance is already quite well established. My wish is to express my gratitude for your efforts on Cedric's behalf. It seems to me that the effect you had on him was precisely the thing he required. While Mother ranks among the finest, most beloved women, her sturdy, pragmatic Scottish practicality was not perpetually capable of comprehending a nature such as my little boy possesses. Whatever she lacked, you provided. Through the efforts of you both, I believe that the instruction Cedric received over this previous two-year period reached a state as close to perfection as possible for a youngster lacking a mother.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0023 }

Everyone enjoys receiving appreciation. Beneath the compliments of Mr. Stanhope, the face of Nell “burst flower like into rosy bloom,” and as he observed her, the occupied, tired worldling believed no girlhood slip had ever appeared fairer or sweeter to him than this small “down east” educator possessing red hair and magnificent eyes.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0024 }

Cedric was positioned in the middle of the two of them, filled with pure joy.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0025 }

“It never entered my mind that father was on his way,” he stated with a beaming face. “Not even Grandma was aware of it. It proved to be a major shock. Usually . . .” Cedric solemnly moved his brown curls from side to side . . . “being surprised isn't to my liking. The entire joy of looking forward to events is stripped away when a surprise happens. However, for an occasion such as this, it works out fine. Father arrived yesterday evening once I was already asleep. Then, when Grandma and Mary Joe were no longer shocked, he and Grandma went to the upper floor to check on me, intending to leave me asleep until daytime. I awoke immediately, though, and spotted father. Believe me, I simply launched myself into his arms.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0026 }

“With an embrace similar to a bear’s,” Mr. Stanhope said, placing his arms around the shoulder of Cedric with a smile. “I scarcely recognized my boy, because he had become so large and tan and strong.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0027 }

“I am not sure whether Grandma or I felt more delighted upon seeing father,” Cedric went on. “Grandma spent the whole day inside the kitchen preparing the food father enjoys eating. She stated that she would not rely on Mary Joe to cook them. Demonstrating joy is done that way by her. Sitting and chatting with father is what I enjoy most. However, provided you will pardon me, I am going to step away from you briefly at present. The cows need to be brought by me for Mary Joe. Doing that counts among my everyday chores.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0028 }

As Cedric scampered off to perform his “daily duty,” Mr. Stanhope conversed with Nell about different subjects. Nell, however, sensed that beneath it all, he was preoccupied with another thought the entire time. Before long, it emerged.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0029 }

“In his final letter, Cedric mentioned traveling alongside you to see a former . . . friend of mine . . . Miss Penrose residing in the stone house located in Welby. Are you well acquainted with her?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0030 }

“Yes, indeed, she is a very dear friend of mine,” Nell answered demurely, betraying nothing of the abrupt sensation that shivered through her whole body upon hearing Mr. Stanhope’s inquiry. Nell “felt instinctively” that a sense of romance was peeking out at her from behind a corner.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0031 }

Getting up and walking over to the window, Mr. Stanhope gazed out at a vast, golden, rolling ocean where a fierce wind played like a harp. A quiet spell fell over the small room with its dark walls for a brief period. He then turned around, a expression that was partly playful and partly affectionate forming a smile as he looked down at Nell’s understanding face.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0032 }

“I am curious about the extent of your knowledge,” he said.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0033 }

“It is all known to me,” Nell answered right away. “The reason being,” she hurried to clarify, “that Miss Rosalind and I share a deep intimacy. Things of so sacred a character would not be disclosed by her to just anyone. Our spirits are kindred.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0034 }

“Yes, it seems to me that you are. Now, I shall request a service from you. Should she permit it, I desire to visit Miss Rosalind. Would you inquire whether she will allow my visit?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0035 }

Was she unwilling? Ah, she certainly was not! Indeed, this was true romance, the genuine article itself, possessing every bit of the enchantment found in verse, tales, and reveries. It might have arrived somewhat late, akin to a blossom opening its petals in October rather than June; yet it remained a rose all the same, overflowing with sweet perfume, its center shining with gold. On her trek through the beech forest to Welby the following day, Nell’s legs had never carried her to a task she desired more. She discovered Miss Rosalind outdoors in the garden. Nell felt terribly worked up. Her fingers turned frigid, and her tone wavered.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0036 }

“I have a piece of news for you, Miss Rosalind . . . a matter of great significance. Are you able to deduce what it might be?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0037 }

It was never expected by Nell that Miss Rosalind might divine it; yet the face of Miss Rosalind turned extremely white, and Miss Rosalind spoke in a calm, hushed tone, out of which had drained all the vibrancy and brilliance that the voice of Miss Rosalind typically brought to mind.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0038 }

“Has Stephen Stanhope returned?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0039 }

“In what manner did you discover this? By whom were you informed?” exclaimed Nell with disappointment, irritated that the major news she had to share was already known.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0040 }

“No one. From your manner of speaking alone, I was certain that had to be the case.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0041 }

“He wishes to visit you,” Nell stated. “Am I permitted to inform him that he can?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0042 }

“Indeed, certainly,” Miss Rosalind fussed nervously. “Nothing prevents him from doing so. His visit is simply that of any former acquaintance.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0043 }

Nell held her own view on the matter while she hurried indoors so as to compose a letter at the desk belonging to Miss Rosalind.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0044 }

“Ah, residing within a tale is truly wonderful,” her cheerful mind reflected. “Naturally, everything is going to end well . . . it has to . . . plus Cedric is going to get a mother just as he desires, bringing joy to everyone. However, Miss Rosalind will be carried off by Mr. Stanhope . . . while the fate of the small stone dwelling remains entirely uncertain . . . which proves that this situation possesses two aspects, just as every single thing in this life appears to have.” After the crucial letter had been composed, Nell personally took it over to the post office in Welby, intercepting the mail carrier there to request that he deliver the message to the office in Brierley.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0045 }

“It’s so very important,” Nell anxiously told him. A messenger of Cupid was hardly reflected in the appearance of the mail carrier, who was quite a crabby old figure; furthermore, Nell felt doubtful about the reliability of his memory. Nevertheless, he promised to make every effort to keep it in mind, leaving her no choice but to be satisfied with his answer.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0046 }

It seemed to Belinda the Fourth that an air of secrecy hung over the stone house that afternoon . . . an enigma that shut her out. Miss Rosalind wandered around the garden in an agitated manner. Nell was likewise overtaken by a spirit of disquiet, pacing back and forth and climbing up and down. Belinda the Fourth put up with this until her endurance reached its limit; at that point, she stood in Nell’s path during the third purposeless journey that fanciful youth made through the kitchen.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0047 }

“Please, Miss Harcourt, ma’am,” said Belinda the Fourth, jerking her extremely blue bows in indignation, “it can easily be noticed that a secret exists between you and Miss Rosalind, and I believe, asking for your forgiveness if I am being overly bold, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, that withholding it from me is truly unkind, considering how close we have all been as friends.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0048 }

“My dear Belinda, were this my own mystery, I would have revealed everything to you . . . yet it belongs to Miss Rosalind, as you understand. Even so, I shall disclose this small amount . . . and provided it leads to nothing, you are required to keep it completely hidden from every single person forever. The reality is that Prince Charming will arrive this evening. Though he appeared in times past, a lapse in judgment caused him to depart and roam in distant places, losing all memory of the hidden route that leads back to the spellbound fortress, the place where the princess kept crying with a loyal heart for his return. At long last, the recollection returned to him, and the princess continues to wait even now . . . for the simple reason that no one except her beloved prince was capable of rescuing her.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0049 }

“Oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, what does that mean in plain language?” the bewildered Belinda gasped.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0050 }

A laugh came from Nell.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0051 }

“Stated plainly, a longtime acquaintance of Miss Rosalind’s is visiting her this evening.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0052 }

“Are you referring to a former suitor of hers?” asked the matter-of-fact Belinda.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0053 }

“In prose . . . that is likely what I intend,” Nell replied solemnly. “Cedric’s father . . . Stephen Stanhope, is the one. And what shall arise from it, goodness only knows, but Belinda, let us anticipate the best outcome.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0054 }

“It’s my hope he weds Miss Rosalind,” Belinda answered without hesitation. “Certain women are meant to be spinsters right from the beginning, and I fear I belong to that group, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, on account of having precious little tolerance for men. Miss Rosalind, however, never was meant for that. I’ve been dreadfully anxious, pondering whatever would become of her once I grew so large that I must depart for Boston. No other girls remain in our family, and heaven only knows what would happen to her if she hired a stranger who could mock her imaginative play, leave items scattered out of place, and refuse to accept the name Belinda the Fifth. She could find a person who wouldn’t prove as unfortunate as I am at smashing crockery, but she’ll never find a single person who’d cherish her more.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0055 }

And with a sniff, the devoted little handmaiden hurried over to the door of the oven.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0056 }

That evening at Echo Cottage, they performed the routine of taking tea, yet not a soul actually consumed any food. Once tea had ended, Miss Rosalind retired to her chamber and dressed in her fresh forget-me-not organdy dress, as Nell styled her hair. Though both were consumed by intense excitement, Miss Rosalind feigned complete composure and apathy.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0057 }

“Tomorrow I am going to have to fix that tear in the drape,” she remarked nervously, examining it as though nothing else mattered at that moment. “For what I spent on them, those drapes ought to have lasted longer. Goodness, Belinda neglected to wipe down the banister once more. I am certainly going to have to address that with her.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0058 }

Stephen Stanhope was walking down the lane and going across the garden while Nell sat on the steps of the porch.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0059 }

“This is the single spot where time stops,” he remarked, sweeping his enchanted gaze over his surroundings. “Not a single detail of this residence or garden has altered from the time I visited a quarter of a century in the past. It restores my youth.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0060 }

“You are aware that time continuously stops inside a magic castle,” Nell remarked gravely. “Things only start occurring once the prince arrives.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0061 }

Mr. Stanhope offered a slightly sorrowful smile down at her upturned face, which shone brightly with youth and potential.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0062 }

“The prince comes too late on occasion,” he stated. He made no request for Nell to render her statement into plain language. Similar to every soulmate, he was one who “understood.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0063 }

“Oh, no, provided he is the genuine prince arriving to see the true princess,” stated Nell, giving her red head a firm shake while opening the door to the parlor. After he entered, she closed it firmly behind him, whereupon she turned to face Belinda the Fourth, who stood in the hallway, entirely composed of “nods and becks and wreathed smiles.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0064 }

“Oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am,” she gasped, “I stole a glance through the kitchen window . . . and he is remarkably handsome . . . and precisely the proper age for Miss Rosalind. And oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, do you suppose there would be any great harm in eavesdropping at the door?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0065 }

“Belinda, it would be awful,” Nell stated decisively, “so you must simply leave with me to escape the lure of temptation.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0066 }

“There is nothing I can do, and remaining here merely waiting is terrible,” Belinda sighed. “What if he fails to propose in the end, Miss Harcourt, ma’am? One can never feel certain about those men. The first Belinda, who is my elder sister, believed she was betrothed to a man at one time. However, it transpired that he held a contrasting view, and she declares she will never place her trust in any of them again. Furthermore, I learned about a different instance in which a man believed he desired one girl terribly much when his true desire was actually her sister the entire time. If a man remains ignorant of his own intentions, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, how can a helpless woman possibly feel certain about them?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0067 }

“To the kitchen we’ll go so we can polish the silver spoons,” Nell said. “Fortunately, that is a job that won’t need a great deal of thought . . . because tonight I couldn’t manage to think. Also, it will help time pass.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0068 }

An hour went by. Following that, at the exact moment Nell set the final gleaming spoon down, the closing of the front door reached their ears. Frightened, each looked to the other’s eyes for reassurance.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0069 }

“Oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am,” Belinda gasped, “if he’s going away this early there’s nothing into it and never will be.” To the window they flew. Going away was not Mr. Stanhope’s intention at all. Down the middle path toward the stone bench, he and Miss Rosalind were strolling slowly.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0070 }

“Oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, his arm is wrapped around her waist,” Belinda the Fourth whispered with delight. “She wouldn't ever permit it unless he has proposed to her.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0071 }

Grabbing Belinda the Fourth around her round waist, Nell spun her about the kitchen until neither of them could breathe.
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0072 }

“Oh, Belinda,” she exclaimed with glee, “I am not a prophetess, nor am I the daughter of one, yet I will offer a prophecy. A wedding will occur within this old stone house prior to the reddening of the maple leaves. Would you like a prose translation of that, Belinda?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0073 }

“Indeed, that makes sense to me,” Belinda remarked. “There is no poetry in a wedding. My goodness, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, tears are falling from your eyes! For what reason?”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0074 }

“Oh, since it is entirely so gorgeous . . . and like a fairy tale . . . and full of romance . . . and sorrowful,” remarked Nell, blinking away the tears from her eyes. “Everything is completely wonderful . . . yet a bit of grief is blended into it as well, in some way.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0075 }

“Oh, naturally taking anyone as a husband carries a risk,” admitted Belinda the Fourth, “yet, taking everything into account, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, plenty of things are far worse than being married.”
{: #nw-v02-c28-p0076 }
